reviews.title: Unused, unusable app and device
reviews.text: I just opened this brand new gift. Had to download an app, hand over my info to create an account, had to get past an device access, told I need to grant access to their AI to connect to wearable, had to get past an I Agree button that I will try to get better sleep, then made it to a screen forcing me into a monthly subscription without option to skip. Said free tier but not possible. When it tried to force me into a subscription via trial intro I closed the app. I now have a useless item I wouldn’t even gift to someone. I can’t believe this is now the worst product experience I can remember ever having.

reviews.title: Device is great. App is essentially broken
reviews.text: The Pulsetto device works very well. The only thing that works about the app is the part that controls the device. Luckily that part is free. But after a month of using the premium features, I can tell you that premium is not worth it—if I weren’t on the free trial, I’d be pretty angry about having to pay for an broken app. They tell you premium is required to sync with Wearables and the Health app, but you can skip paying for it because the sync is broken anyway. When it does work, the data it imports doesn’t match up to what you see in your wearable app so the “insights” are meaningless. And now the outbound sync TO Health and my Whoop app just randomly stopped working. Tech support is all nice, sincere people, but they DON’T. EVER. FIX. ANYTHING. And sometimes the directions and advice they give seems aimed at the Android version. They keep giving me the same script over and over again. I deleted and reinstalled the app several times on their advice. I’m not tech-challenged, either. If I even bother contacting support, it’s because I’ve exhausted every possible way to try and fix it on my own. The problem with this app is that they don’t know how to fix it either. Finally one of them admitted to me that all of the premium features are still in beta. That’s right—they expect you to buy a subscription for unfinished, untested software. I am old enough to remember when software companies either paid you to beta test or at least gave you free beta-test copies. Not these guys. They advertise a finished product, and want you to buy it AND test it for them. And given that none of the paid features actually work, even calling it beta is being generous. If all you care about is making the Pulsetto device go, then this app works perfectly, and you won’t need premium. If you want any data or insights, you have to pay. But don’t bother doing that, because it won’t work.

reviews.text: The new app update makes everything more complicated. Now it takes multiple presses for features that used to be one step away. Like changing the intensity used to just be pressing plus or minus, now you have to open a menu and slide the intensity level over. It is WAY more annoying because you can’t just start at full intensity. Seriously do your app designers even use your own product? Change the app back this new one is terrible.

reviews.title: Like it but
reviews.text: It tries to sell you the premium app version constantly.

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text: To begin with, I was upset to find out that the device won’t work without using Bluetooth and an App, but I really wanted to see if it will help my anxiety. The app logs me out at least once a week, which is annoying. I wish there was the option to turn off the light all together  because it’s quite an interruption if you are trying to use it before falling asleep. Even on the lowest setting, the light is really bright. It seems that the stimulation is the same for all options (stress, calm, sleep, pain all feel the same). I do like the meditation and music features. And I do like that you can add more time since 4 minutes just doesn’t seem like enough for me.

reviews.title: Vaguely disreputable
reviews.text: The amount of positive reviews is for the device NOT the app. I hate the amount of pop ups I have to deal with just to use my device. I HATE buying something and then needing to buy a yearly subscription just to use the dang thing, though. Plus there are two different prices offered in the pop ups which show to me that this company is money grubbing and vaguely disreputable and that annoys me, too. Love the actual device though. Such a shame about how the actual company runs, though. Plus support didn’t actually support me with what I needed and was ai assisted so it gave me a whole bunch of information about slightly related and tangential issues and was more of another thing to manage then was helpful. Think twice before purchasing this particular device, although I LOVE the actual device itself but there might be others that don’t need apps (imagine that??? Probably not though🙄) or include subscriptions with the cost of device🤷🏻‍♀️

reviews.title: Helps with disabilities
reviews.text: I am recovering from cushings disease which is an overproduction of cortisol that causes lots of issues. After my surgery I developed pots which is when your nervous system does not control your cardiovascular system correctly.  I haven’t been able to work in a long time and I routinely wake up nauseous because of the pots. This not only helps lower my cortisol but it also helps regulate the pots and I can sit up better concentrate better and maybe I’ll be able to go back to work soon.

reviews.title: Expensive device, limited free use
reviews.text:
I’ve add the Pulsetto device for about 7 months now.

My biggest concern is the continuous removal of free in app features that you now need to pay for. I first lost access to guided breathing during a session. While the Pulsetto effect is yet to be proven, breathing is known to help reduce stress.

The latest update removed access to soundtrack during a session. This one makes no sense at all. 

I also lost access to the personal session and now if I want to use my $300+ Pulsetto device for the stress management program in app (what I originally bought it for) I need to pay extra every month.

Customer service was quite inefficient when I first got started in helping address in app bugs.

On the efficacy side: no effect on gut related issues.

I do not recommend Pulsetto and will look for another device and a company who supports its customer in line with their claimed mission.

reviews.title: Just a tens device No “Braingasm” as advertised
reviews.text: Just a very expensive tens device. No “Braingasm” as advertised.  Feels somewhat relaxing but not what was advertised and fries not lower blood pressure which is why I sacrificed to buy this. I regret spending so much money.  It’s nothing special just slick marketing.

reviews.title: Watch out for subscription
reviews.text: The device itself is great. The app, even if you cancel within the free trial, will bill you for a premium subscription and the response to cancel the subscription is not good. I was charged this morning and all communication has been about what the premium program does, despite multiple attempts to reverse a charge that never should have happened. I would be happy to share screenshots with anyone interested of my experience.

reviews.title: Unnecessary App
reviews.text: I like the Pulsetto device, but I just want it to have an on and off switch, not have to be run through an app. There have been times the app doesn’t work so I can’t use the device. The different “stimulations” modes in the app (like sleep, stress, etc.) are literally just different amounts of time—sleep is 10 minutes, stress is 4 minutes, etc. And again, even with the app, no on/off switch or option to set your own number of minutes, which is such an artificial construct, like they’re just trying to invent a reason to justify a whole app. Even the device levels are really subjective, they totally depend on the amount of electrode gel you’re using. I don’t know why anyone would pay a whopping $99/year for a premium version of the app. A ridiculous money grab.

reviews.title: Won’t stay online…
reviews.text:
So irritating - definitely does not make me feel calm with this one - 
As of lately, when the app goes from my Wi-Fi to my cell service, it goes into off-line mode. 
*Unfortunately, it never goes back online! Even when I hook back up to my Wi-Fi.
*There is no way to get it back online when it is in this “offline mode” state!
*When that happens, guess what my 20 minute session does it shows as not finished and gives me a zero.
* do you know how frustrating this is?
This is the exact opposite of what the Pulsetto should do.

reviews.title: Great for POTA
reviews.text: This was recommended to me by the POTS clinic at Johns Hopkins.  I was highly skeptical, however, it has really helped me recover from activities that would otherwise throw me into a flare.  I really wish that they would expand the pairing to other wearables.  I also use the visible band to manage my illness.  I think these two devices working together make a lot of sense.

reviews.title: Application Offline
reviews.text: Performed my second session of the day and when I woke up in the morning, I never received credit for the session. It looks like I need to start over at day one instead of day fourteen. Obviously the cloud servers were running some kind of maintenance. Not sure why they do not allow me to fix my session count in the app.

reviews.title: Really good
reviews.text: I love the hardware, and the app is great. I give 4 stars because you will be charged $50 a couple weeks after you receive the device if you don’t go in and unsubscribe from the premium app. You are made aware of the fact by an email created by AI and it can’t be reasoned with and it can’t tell you anything about how to unsubscribe. So - $50 lighter and a bit smarter so TOTALLY WORTH IT (sarcasm). Anyway, as for positives - it works great and the standard app (no premium) is very good at controlling the device and has all the features I need. If you need premium, the good news is you’re signed up for it from day 1. Other positives - I am sleeping better, my HRV has increased and my stress level are down. Exactly what I bought this for. So - thanks for making all this, but don’t take any more money from me.
